notes: Overturn confirmed, as PARTIAL: the exclusion half (COPY refused, COBOL7006) is right and the admission half refuses legal source. SR6 admits any single COBOL word but COPY, and a reserved word is a COBOL word (IV.4.2.2.1), so BY, LEADING and TRAILING are legal word-1 and word-2. The 1985 REPLACING format has no LEADING/TRAILING partial-word phrase, so at --std 85 those two are ordinary words in an operand position. The format alternates operand BY operand, so the position, not the spelling, says which BY is the keyword. Rerun: s14 (REPLACING BY BY "B") and s7 are COBOL2449 'a REPLACING operand is missing'; s16 (REPLACING TRAILING BY "B") is COBOL0900 (partial-word phrase requires COBOL-2002) plus COBOL2449; control s11 runs START/Q/END. Own probes separate the replacement from the operand reader: h1 (REPLACING ==BY== BY =="B"==) and h2 (REPLACING ==TRAILING== BY =="B"==) both run START / AB / END, so the replacing engine matches these words and only ReadOperand (any BY where an operand is expected is taken as missing) and ParseReplacingOperands (LEADING/TRAILING read as the 2002 phrase at every edition) refuse them. Note PB5418 is right in citation, sites, expected results (s14 and s16 print AB) and harm flags (rejects_legal_source, MINOR). kb/Work PB5418 holds the defect (adjudication: held-85/set7/decisions.json).

next.reason: 1985: "Word-1 or word-2 may be any single COBOL word except 'COPY'."; 2023: "No word-1/word-2 operand; the 7.2.3.3 syntax rules cover only pseudo-text-1/2 and partial-word-1/2 for REPLACING". The 2023 COPY syntax rules define only pseudo-text and partial-word REPLACING operands, so the word operand and its COPY restriction are gone. GR-13 is a different, broader rule.
